sources.entry: Personal Management System - Organize the essentials of everyday life, everything from a simple to-do list, and notes up to payments, and schedules. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: A self-hosted personal management system backend that organizes everyday life data such as to-dos, notes, contacts, passwords, payments, schedules and files.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a backend-only application for managing personal data, modeled loosely on a CMS or CRM, and designed to be extended with new modules. It offers modules for goals/todos, notes, contacts, encrypted passwords, health records (illnesses, doctors, appointments), achievements, recurring schedules, ongoing issues with sub-records, travel ideas with map links and images, and payments (including monthly summaries, product price tracking, owed money and bills). Other modules cover shopping lists, job tracking (after-hours and holiday days), masonry photo galleries, a file table with rename/download/remove, video storage, and read-only reports built from database data. Schedule entries are shown on the dashboard and in a notification bell. The author states the goal is to run it 24/7 on a home network without internet access.
use_cases: track personal payments and monthly spending
manage recurring reminders like car oil changes or bills
keep contacts organized and backed up
organize personal photo galleries and scanned documents
keep a self-hosted personal dashboard on a home server
how_to_run: Check the official documentation linked from the README for installation steps
stack: PHP (inferred from backend-only web app; not explicitly named in README)
notable: Backend only; a separate frontend is linked from the documentation
Passwords are stored encrypted in the database and can be copied back in plain form from the frontend
Extensible module design intended for users with development knowledge to add their own modules
Demo login available (admin@admin.admin) per the README
caveats: Author states no guarantee of support and limited time for maintenance
Setup details are not in the README; it points to external documentation
Frontend is separate from this backend repository
